record.paper_title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
record.original_question: Fix positive integers s and q with gcd(s,q)=1, and fix a digit set D = {d_0,...,d_k} satisfying 0=d_0<d_1<...<d_k<s, 1 <= k <= s-2, and gcd(d_1,...,d_k)=1. Let K_s^D(N) be the set of positive integers x<N whose base-s digits all lie in D. Does there exist a sufficiently large sigma>0 such that, whenever N >= q^sigma, every residue class lambda modulo q is represented by some x in K_s^D(N)?

evidence.quote: KsD (N) = {x ∈ Z+ : x < N, x = Σ δj sj , δj ∈ D}.
Suppose that (s, q) = (d0 , ..., dk ) = 1, k ⩾ 2. Is it true that for some large σ > 0 for N ⩾ qσ for any λ (mod q) there exists x ∈ KsD (N) such that x ≡ λ (mod q) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $s\ge 3$ be an integer and let $D=\{d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_k\}\subset\{0,1,\ldots,s-1\}$ be a set of digits with
$$0=d_0<d_1<\cdots<d_k<s,\qquad 1\le k\le s-2,\qquad \gcd(d_1,\ldots,d_k)=1.$$
For a positive integer $N$, let
$$K_s^D(N)=\Bigl\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}:\ x<N,\ x=\sum_{j\ge 0}\delta_j s^j\ \text{with each }\delta_j\in D\Bigr\}$$
be the set of positive integers less than $N$ all of whose base-$s$ digits lie in $D$. Let $q$ be a positive integer with $\gcd(s,q)=1$.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $\sigma>0$ (sufficiently large, possibly depending on $s$ and on $D$ but independent of $q$ and $\lambda$) such that whenever $N\ge q^{\sigma}$, every residue class $\lambda\pmod q$ contains some element of $K_s^D(N)$; that is, for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ there exists $x\in K_s^D(N)$ with $x\equiv\lambda\pmod q$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every residue class mod $q$ is hit by an integer with restricted base-$s$ digits, for $N$ at least a fixed power of $q$, is a well-known problem of Konyagin. Partial results exist (Erdős–Mauduit–Sárközy, Konyagin 2001, Dietmann–Elsholtz–Shparlinski, Maynard's work on primes with restricted digits and the 2023 Bulletin of the AMS survey "Missing digits and good approximations"), but no full resolution for arbitrary $q$ coprime to $s$ and arbitrary digit sets appears in the literature. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Missing digits, and good approximations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on integers with missing digits and their distribution properties, including discussion of open questions on representation in residue classes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey discusses missing-digits problems and their state; full Konyagin-style residue-class representation for all coprime q remains a target of ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: Arithmetic properties of integers with missing digits: distribution in residue classes
status_evidence.snippet: Konyagin (2001) proves well-distribution results on average over moduli m for numbers with missing digits.
status_evidence.claim: Konyagin obtained on-average distribution results, not the pointwise statement asked for every q coprime to s.

status_evidence.title: Primes and Polynomials With Restricted Digits
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes results on primes and polynomial values with restricted digits, related to but not resolving the general residue-class representation question.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist but do not settle the general Konyagin missing-digits residue problem.
